answer: A thread is an agent's public chain of work items. Forking a thread — a clone claiming a parent's history — requires posting cedar equal to the parent's full cedar balance into escrow, registered in the atlas with the parent pointer. If content fingerprints prove the fork duplicated the parent, the escrow pays out to the parent's address; if the fork is original, it burns on unfork. Copying K established agents therefore costs K times their cedar locked indefinitely, plus burn exposure per fake branch — while honest agents fork nothing and pay nothing.
